about: RIVER-WATER TEST (chat 9, Oct 28 2026; chat 8's KPC_OwnLandLayers_Rivers_desk.md section 2): does an ownership layer HIT a point on the water inside its unit? One runner pass, 1 request / 2 s. A NO HIT only proves 'cuts the river out' if the point is truly inside the unit: points marked (chat 9) were picked from the river course and are approximate, and none was checked against the unit's outer boundary in this pass.

summary.NPS tracts: Green River in Mammoth Cave: all 3 points HIT (2 x MACA-01-101 'Federal Land (Fee)'; Dennison Ferry reach = MACA-08-119 'Private' tract): the NPS tract layer KEEPS the river. New River Gorge + Big South Fork desk points: NO HIT (check the points are inside those units).
summary.FWS realty: Ohio River Islands channel, Cache River (AR), Detroit River: all NO HIT. Ohio River Islands NWR is islands only, so its channel is not refuge land; Cache + Detroit points are approximate: re-test with points taken inside the refuge polygon.
summary.FS Basic Ownership: Red River gorge channel, Cumberland River in DBNF, Manistee River: all NO HIT = Basic Ownership appears to CUT rivers out (or the points fall on non-FS land): confirm with the proclamation boundary.
summary.Ohio DNR: Mosquito Lake mid-lake: NO HIT on nolakes /5 + /7 (expected: 'no lakes') AND on ODNR_ODNR_Lands_External; ODNR_Lands_Dissolved could not be read (no polygon layer listed).
summary.Michigan DNR: Lake Michigan at Warren Dunes = HIT (Warren Dunes State Park): the parks layer KEEPS the water. Manistee River point = NO HIT (expected: Forest Service land, not a state park).
